Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed for both food quality and service. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|-----------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, spicy broth) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Baan Thai** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, peanuts)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Thai Orchid** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Siam Square** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, spicy broth) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Thai House** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, peanuts)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants are located on the same block (1220 W 18th St), so you can easily walk between them if you want to try a few different dishes. They’re all in the West Loop, a vibrant neighborhood with plenty of other dining options. ### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Dining at Thai Restaurants 1. **Ask for “no egg” and “no fish sauce.”** Many Thai dishes contain egg or fish sauce as a base; simply request these ingredients be omitted. 2. **Look for “tofu” or “vegetable” versions.** Most Thai menus will label vegetarian dishes with tofu or a vegetable icon. 3. **Check the “vegetarian” or “vegan” section.** Some restaurants have a dedicated vegetarian menu that lists all plant‑based options. 4. **Use the “vegetarian” emoji (🥗) on the menu.** Many modern Thai restaurants mark vegetarian items with a green leaf or salad emoji. 5. **Call ahead if you have specific dietary restrictions.** While most places are accommodating, it’s always good to confirm that they can meet your needs. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like reservations or more detailed menu information, let me know and I can help you look up the latest details.
